memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Two sons were born to Eber: One was named Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided; his brother was named Joktan. Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah... - Gen 10:25-27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Tucked into this genealogy is an intriguing note: a son was named Peleg, "because in his time the earth was divided." This likely points ahead to the scattering of peoples at Babel, which the next chapter describes. Even in a simple naming, Scripture is quietly weaving the larger story of how the nations came to be spread across the earth. God was at work in the dividing, just as He is at work in the gathering.

There is something worth pausing on here. The division and scattering of peoples, which we will soon read came through human pride at Babel, is nonetheless woven into God's unfolding plan. What humans intended one way, God was using for His own purposes - spreading humanity across the earth to fill it, just as He had commanded.

This is a comfort when we face division and scattering in our own lives and world. Families are divided, communities scattered, relationships fractured. Yet God is not absent from these hard realities. He is able to work even through division to accomplish His good purposes, weaving our scattered stories into His larger design.

And the gospel points to a glorious reversal of all division. What was scattered at Babel begins to be regathered at Pentecost, when people of every language heard the good news in their own tongue (Acts 2:5-11). And one day, the scattered nations will be fully gathered as one people before God's throne (Rev 7:9). The God who was present in the dividing is the God who is gathering His people home.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Where do you see division or scattering in your life or world?
- Can you trust that God is at work even through division for His purposes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that even in division and scattering, You are at work for good. Comfort me where I feel fractured or scattered, and thank You that in Christ You are gathering Your people into one.
